title: Child, Amidst the Flowers at Play
description: Child, Amidst the Flowers at Play in Tonic Solfa to HEINLEIN, doh is F: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 5 verses and a piano.
about: Felicia Hemans wrote these words. They were printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1848), as hymn 98, “All Must Pray”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Sevens (7.7.7.7) (7.7.7.7), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to HEINLEIN; any other Sevens (7.7.7.7) tune fits them as well.
underlay: Child, a-midst the flowers at play, While the red light fades a-way; Moth-er, with thine ear-nest eye, Ev-er fol-lowing si-lent-ly;

lines: Child, amidst the flowers at play,
While the red light fades away;
Mother, with thine earnest eye,
Ever following silently;
Father, by the breeze of eve
Called thy daily toil to leave;
Pray! ere yet the dark hours be,
Lift the heart, and bend the knee!
Traveller in the stranger's land,
Far from thine own household band;
Mourner, haunted by the tone
Of a voice from this world gone;
Captive, in whose narrow cell
Sunshine hath not leave to dwell;
Sailor, on the darkening sea,
Lift the heart, and bend the knee!
Ye that triumph, ye that sigh,
Kindred by one holy tie,
Heaven's first star alike ye see;
Lift the heart, and bend the knee!

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: Felicia Hemans died in 1835.
credits: Words by Felicia Hemans (1793–1835), public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848); set to HEINLEIN by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
